summary.text: Andy Barr is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Kentucky and the U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 6th District, which he has held since 2013. A Lexington attorney by training, he worked in the Fletcher state administration before winning his House seat.
He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Daniel Cameron with 60.5% of the vote and describes himself as a conservative ally of President Trump.

paragraphs.text: Barr was born in Lexington, Kentucky, in 1973, and graduated from Henry Clay High School in 1992.
He received a B.A. in government and philosophy from the University of Virginia in 1996 and a J.D. from the University of Kentucky College of Law in 2001.

He worked as a legislative assistant to Rep. Jim Talent (R-Mo.), then as an attorney, a part-time law professor at Morehead State University, and deputy general counsel to Kentucky Gov. Ernie Fletcher.
He returned to private legal practice in 2008 and also taught constitutional law part-time at the University of Kentucky.
Barr lost his first House race in 2010 to Democratic Rep. Ben Chandler by about 650 votes, 49.8% to 50.1%.
He won a rematch in 2012, defeating Chandler 50.6% to 46.7% in Kentucky's 6th District, and took office in 2013.
He was re-elected in 2018, defeating Amy McGrath 51.0% to 47.8%.

Ballotpedia lists his 2025-2026 House assignments as the Financial Services and Foreign Affairs committees and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and notes that he chaired the Financial Institutions and Monetary Policy Subcommittee in 2023-2024.
His campaign website says he wrote a bill to block Biden administration ESG mandates for retirement accounts that became the first veto of Joe Biden's presidency.
Sen. Mitch McConnell announced on February 20, 2025, that he would not seek re-election, leaving the seat open, and Barr announced on April 22, 2025, that he would run for it.
He won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary over Daniel Cameron (30.8%) and others.
According to his campaign website, Barr lives in Lexington with his wife, Davis, and their four children.
